name: Foundation for Perfection .docx
text:
Foundation for Perfection:
Learning How to Eliminate Resistance When Doing a Job
Achieving the Training Trifecta:  Temperament, Foundation, Task Completion 

What is your “Training Through Process”?
Traditional (Give to Pressure) – Horse Trainer (Drilling & Repetitions) 
Forcing the Body (Head and Neck, Front Feet, Hind Feet)
Chemical in the Body:  Cortisol 
Alternative (Seeking Relief) – Horse Teacher (Discovery and Revelations) 
Influencing the Soul (Mind, Will and Emotions) 
Understanding Identity (Driving Factors) 
Chemical in the Body:  Endorphins (Dopamine/ Serotonin) 

3 Causes of Resistance
       1)  LACK OF COMMUNICAITON  
           - Horse needs more time, patience, teaching (Slow down!) 
        2)  FEAR
          - Self-preservation shown through FEAR 
   - Due to lack of Confidence (Slow down and build confidence!) 
        3)  RESENTMENT 
   -  Self-preservation shown through RESENTMENT 
   -  Due to false teaching, unwilling submission & unbalanced life to direction ratio.  
 
5 Factors to Eliminate Resistance

1)  WILLING SUBMISSION– After an initial cue, the horse performs the task on a loose rein and with no leg pressure.  “It is the horse’s idea.” 
 
 2)  GOOD COMMUNICATION – Learning to read, feel, and understand what the horse is saying in response to our request (Communication involves two individuals, what is the horse saying?).  We communicate with horses through their primary driving factors, underlying driving factors and feel, timing, and balance.
3 Primary Driving Factors:  Self-preservation, Comfort, and Companionship
Prey Animal, Herbivore (Graze 17hrs/day), Environment, Herd Animal 
      2 Underlying Factors:  Confidence, and Energy (motivation and determination)
1 Variable Factor:  Hormones

3)  BALANCED LIFE TO DIRECTION RATIO – The ratio is determined by the speed which we can willingly bring the life up and willingly direct it on set line (straight or curved), without losing “direction.”
Life – The ability to move the horse, with any given speed at any given time. 
 Direction – When the slack is taken out of the rein, the horse puts the      
                          slack back in The rein with suppleness through the poll and 
                          loin.    


Horizontal Direction – (Axis Vertebrae) – Left to right

          3 Signs – Poll 
Break in the poll horizontally (hairline curves between 
      the ears)
Nose directly underneath the eye 
Ears stay flat (No head tilting)
 4)  Should not see any white in the eye (looking back not 
                              forward) 
          3 Signs – Loin
5)  Front feet and hind feet travel on same path as the nose
6)  Outside hind steps out, inside hind steps up underneath the navel
7)  Poll and loin should make a perfect “C” around rider’s leg
8)  Should be able to ride a perfect circle (“O” is half of a “C”)   

              b)  Vertical Direction – (Atlas Vertebrae) – Up and down
- Break in the poll vertically; nose should be perpendicular to the ground.   

 Four Levels of Directed Life   
        1)  Submit the life (Stage 1 Mechanical Foundation)
        2)  Fill them with life (With no signs of self-preservation)
        3)  Direct the life (1st Straight lines, 2nd Curved lines)  
        4)  Led by the life (Stage 2 Mechanical Foundation)
        (Life = Body (Hindquarters) & Soul (Mind, Will & Emotions)

4)  SOLID FOUNDATION OF MANUEVERS- Ability to move the horse feet in any direction to accomplish any job. 
Stage 1 – Stop the inside front foot and walk the other feet forward 
                          around it.   
Stage 2 – Hindquarters pulling the horse in a reverse motion.
Stage 3 – Lateral movement of front feet and hind feet together.
Stage 4 – Stop the inside hind foot and walk the other feet forward 
                          around it.   

5)  PHASES OF TRAINING:  FOUNDATION TO FINISH 
   1) Setting the Foundation:  
            - Horizontal/ Vertical Direction & 4 Stages w/ Willing Submission 
   2) Building the Foundation through Doing Jobs:
            -  Sacrifice the job to build on the foundation
   3) Testing the Foundation  
            - Sacrifice the Foundation to do the job (Finding the holes) 
   4) Using and Maintaining the Foundation while doing jobs:
            - Goal of the FFP:  Attaining the “Training Trifecta”

1) Good to catch
-3 -2 -1 0 +1 +2 +3
Driving Factors (3 primary, 2 underlying, 1 variable)
- Self-preservation, Comfort, Companionship
- Confidence, Energy
- Hormones (mares and stallions)
2) Stage 1 w/ Willing Submission (In a crisis)
(standing and walking)
-3 -2 -1 0 +1 +2 +3
1) Self-preservation (fight or flight)
High Low
-3 -2 -1 0 +1 +2 +3
3) Horizontal Direction (standing and walking,)
-3 -2 -1 0 +1 +2 +3
2) Confidence
Low High
-3 -2 -1 0 +1 +2 +3
4) Stage 2 w/ Willing Submission
-3 -2 -1 0 +1 +2 +3
3) Willingness (response to request)
Resistant Willing
-3 -2 -1 0 +1 +2 +3
5) Stage 3 w/ Willing Submission
-3 -2 -1 0 +1 +2 +3
4) Reaction to social separation
Nervous Calm
-3 -2 -1 0 +1 +2 +3
6) Stage 4 w/ Willing Submission
-3 -2 -1 0 +1 +2 +3
5) Energy (motivation and determination)
Low High (Ready for Client)
-3 -2 -1 0 +1 +2 +3
7) Lead w/ Willing Submission and Respect
-3 -2 -1 0 +1 +2 +3
6) Sensitivity (response to light pressure )
Dull Responsive (Ready for Client)
-3 -2 -1 0 +1 +2 +3
8) Pick up feet
-3 -2 -1 0 +1 +2 +3
To accomplish weekly task completions a horse’s driving
factors must be “in order”.
Remember to follow the Training Trifecta: Foundation
Temperament, then Task Completion.
“A” (Found) + “B” (Temp) = “C” (Task Comp.)
